evidence.text: Q3 fuel very likely came in above AAL's $3.75/gal guide assumption: Alaska, which also assumed $3.75, reported $3.94, and United reported $3.90. AAL's CFO puts each 1c/gal at about $10m a quarter, so $0.15-0.19 above plan is about $150-190m, or roughly $0.23-0.29 a share, against the guide. Consensus of -$0.28 already sits above the -$0.40 guide midpoint, so it assumes revenue at the top of the +16-19% range will offset that fuel cost.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (23 Jul): an adjusted EPS beat ($0.15 against about $0.03) was sold -8.3% on the guide cut. Q1 2026: a beat on the adjusted loss (-$0.40 against -$0.47) gave +2.4% on the baseline window (about +5% intraday per press). The reported quarter has mattered less than the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Zacks shows a -2.66% Earnings ESP and consensus revisions down sharply over 60 days, so the street knows fuel ran hot. But a consensus of -$0.28, above the guide midpoint, implies analysts expect revenue upside to absorb all of it. If the market had fully priced the fuel overrun, consensus would sit at or below -$0.40.
evidence.independence: United Q3 fuel $3.90/gal (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000184/ual_erx09302026xex991.htm). On the offsetting side, AAL's CEO said on 16 Sept that he felt 'really good' about +16-19% revenue (https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/09/16/breaking-news/american-and-united-prepare-capacity-cuts-over-fuel-costs/). Proxy: peer fuel, not AAL's own number.

evidence.text: The Q4 guide and the FY 2026 guide (-$0.65 to +$0.65, implied Q4 midpoint about +$0.65 after Q1 -$0.40, Q2 +$0.15 and a Q3 midpoint of -$0.40) will absorb a large fuel step-up. AAL's CFO said on 16 Sept 2026 that Q4 fuel was running about $1/gal above the July assumption, about $1bn of extra cost. Peers have since guided Q4 fuel at $4.80 (United, which said this is about 45c above the street's fuel deck) and $4.65-4.85 (Alaska, which guided a Q4 loss of -$2.50 to -$2.00). At about 1.05bn Q4 gallons, a 45c gap to the street's deck is about $470m, roughly $0.70 a share for AAL before fare recapture, so the Q4 guide and a cut FY range likely land below current models.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: AAL has sold fuel-driven guide cuts hard: -8.3% on 2026-07-23 (FY cut to -$0.65/+$0.65 despite a Q2 beat). The baseline's Jan/Jul prints (-7.0%, -9.6%, -8.7%) were also negative and its Oct/Apr prints positive (+5.6%, +2.4%, +3.1%), though the season pattern is not established.
evidence.why_not_priced: The CFO's +$1/gal is public, and UAL's statement that its $4.80 sits 45c above the street deck says sell-side fuel assumptions lag the curve. If AAL's Q4 consensus had been rebased to about $4.80 fuel, analysts would be sitting on a Q4 loss and an FY loss well below the guide's midpoint, and no source found shows that. No sourced AAL Q4/FY consensus was found, so this is capped. The put skew of +4.5 already pays for downside, which is why this is sized below the July reaction.
evidence.independence: UAL Q4 fuel $4.80, 45c above the consensus deck (https://www.aol.com/articles/united-airlines-forecasts-fourth-quarter-200743000.html, 2026-10-20). Alaska Q4 fuel $4.65-4.85 and a Q4 loss guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000766421/000076642126000046/ex99110202026earningsrelea.htm). Delta Q4 fuel about $4.25 (refinery offset) and FY cut to $5.10-5.60 (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx). Gulf Coast jet spot peaked at $4.705 on 15 Sept and was $4.399 on 29 Sept (https://www.flycraft.com/jet-fuel-price).

evidence.text: The peer reaction template this week is that fuel-driven guide misses are being looked through when revenue pass-through is visible. United guided Q4 adjusted EPS to $0.50-1.50 against $1.76 consensus (midpoint 43% below) with Q4 revenue growth over 20% and 72% fuel recapture, and its stock rose about 4.9-6.9% on 21 Oct. Delta fell only about 3% on 9 Oct after cutting FY EPS from $6.50-7.50 to $5.10-5.60. AAL, at 30% below its 52-week high with puts heavily bid, can see a guide in line with peers' trigger the same relief.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July 2026 the peer read did not save AAL (-8.3%). In Oct 2025 AAL rose +5.6% on its print. AAL tends to move about 1.2-1.5x UAL on sector news (high beta, levered), which is not sourced here and is an inference.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: AAL is +7% over 5 days and rallied with UAL today, the baseline sealed at 17:11 UTC. But the option market still pays +4.5 vol points for puts, with put/call open interest at 3.68. If the market had accepted the UAL template for AAL, the skew would have flattened and the implied move would sit nearer the 7% historical median, not 5.6%.
evidence.independence: Investing.com 21 Oct: UAL's Q4 guide was 43% below consensus, Evercore kept its Outperform, and the ticker showed UAL +6.9% (https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-united-airlines-stock-sliding-today-93CH-5644458). DAL's -3% on its cut (rttnews above). Shares the UAL guide document with finding 2 (one reads the number, this reads the reaction).

evidence.text: Revenue and capacity support a strong Q4 revenue guide and a better Q3 top line. AAL's CEO said on 16 Sept that revenue strength was broad-based (domestic and international, premium and coach) and that AAL had recaptured 'a tremendous amount' of fuel. AAL is trimming Q4/December capacity and exited six NY-area routes in October. Domestic-heavy peers printed strong numbers: United domestic passenger revenue +19.9% and TRASM +15.9%, Delta domestic unit revenue +16%, Alaska RASM +11.7% (beating) with September yield +17%. Delta and United both guide Q4 revenue about +20% or more.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: record revenue +16.3% did not stop a -8.3% move, because fuel guidance dominated. Q1 2026: record revenue plus a beat bought about +2.4-5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus of $16.2bn already sits at the top of AAL's Q3 range, so Q3 revenue is largely priced. What is not obviously priced is a Q4 revenue guide near +20%, since AAL's Q3 guide was +16-19% on +3-5% capacity, and Q4 capacity is being cut. If it were priced, the downside skew would be smaller.
evidence.independence: United domestic +19.9% and TRASM +15.9% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000184/ual_erx09302026xex991.htm). Delta domestic unit revenue +16% and Q4 seats under 2% (rttnews above). Alaska September yield +17% (ALK 8-K above). AAL route exits (https://liveandletsfly.com/american-airlines-q3-2026-earnings-preview/). Shares the 16 Sept Reuters piece with finding 2.

evidence.text: Balance sheet: total debt $34.7bn, stockholders' deficit $3.97bn and liquidity $11.3bn at end-Q2. With FY EPS likely turning to a loss on about $1bn+ of extra Q4 fuel, the free-cash-flow outlook and the debt-reduction path are at risk of a downgrade on the call. AAL is the most levered equity of the big three, so FCF commentary carries more weight here than at DAL or UAL.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable in the baseline; leverage was cited in the 2025 downgrades (Goldman Sell at $8, April 2025), per older coverage.
evidence.why_not_priced: The debt figures are public, and the stock's -23% YTD (against DAL +8%) reflects leverage. What is not public is the new FCF number. Delta cut its FCF to about $2.5bn from $3-4bn. If AAL's FCF turn negative were priced, the stock would not have joined the UAL rally today. Note there is no new financing event, so [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: Delta's FCF cut (rttnews above) is the peer analogue. The debt figures share a document with finding 4's capacity data (Live and Let's Fly cites $28.9bn LTD and $3.1bn current).

evidence.text: Q3 seasonality and argenx's beat pattern point to Q3 product net sales near $1.72-1.77B against an aggregator total-revenue bar of $1.57-1.65B. The pattern: Q3'25 added +$178M QoQ (to $1,127M) after Q2'25's +$159M. Q2'26 added +$219M QoQ (to $1,516M, +17%). Q3'25 beat consensus ($1.151B against $1.056B, about +9%) and Q2'26 beat it ($1.516B against $1.42B, about +7%). Repeating even a +$200M Q3 addition gives about $1.72B, roughly 4-10% above the bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3'25 revenue beat (about +9%): stock +5.75% pre-market on 2025-10-30 (https://www.itiger.com/news/1117828768). Q2'26 beat (about +7%): +5% early in Brussels, +8.6% at the day-0 close (baseline row 2026-07-23 +8.56%). Q1'26 ($1.298B, flat QoQ): -2.5% (https://stocktitan.net/news/ARGX/argenx-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provides-d857iu0zibsu.html). Beats on this line have been bought.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the street were modelling the usual Q3 step-up, the aggregator bar would sit near $1.75B, not $1.57-1.65B; the bar implies only +4% to +9% QoQ, below every recent sequential add. The October tape has been driven by the UNITY futility news (-11.8%) and its rebound, not by sales expectations. The caveat: this is my extrapolation from company history, not a script series, and the bar itself is disputed.
evidence.independence: Two company releases (Q3'25 and Q2'26) give the sequential pattern. Consensus-beat sizes come from separate press (itiger/Stock Track for Q3'25, Saxo for Q2'26). A May 2026 FY26 Vyvgart model of about $6.5B (https://ca.investing.com/news/-4646284) implies a higher H2 run-rate than the $1.65B bar. No IQVIA script data was found.

evidence.text: Q3 2026 is the first full quarter of the all-serotype gMG label (FDA approval 2026-05-08, which adds about 11,000 addressable US patients). On the Q2 call the company said payer policies already covered about 55% of US commercial lives within 10 weeks and most plans were removing serology requirements, and that about 80% of Q2 US prefilled-syringe patients were new to VYVGART. These demand drivers were only partly in Q2 numbers.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Label-driven sales acceleration was the stated driver of the Q2'26 beat, which bought +5% to +8.6%. A separate line-level reaction is not isolable.
evidence.why_not_priced: These are public call statements, so they are partly priced. They matter only through the size of the Q3 sequential add, which the low aggregator bar suggests is not fully modelled. If they were priced, the bar would already sit at or above the Q2 sequential pace.
evidence.independence: This shares the Q3 sales line with finding 1 but rests on different facts (the label approval and payer coverage, not the seasonal pattern). Sized small for that reason.

evidence.text: Into the print the stock rebounded +8.27% in five sessions, from about $818 (the 2026-10-08 close after the -11.8% UNITY Sjögren's futility drop, and the 10-14 close per biopharmawatch) to $886. A remeasurement of argenx's pre-existing Forte stake and added FB102 R&D are possible below-the-line or opex noise against the $7.44 EPS bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent acquisition of this size in argenx's recent prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: The deal is public. What is not visible is how it is accounted for in Q3 (capitalised IPR&D or business combination, any stake remeasurement, deal costs). Aggregator EPS ranges ($6.51-$7.44) suggest models differ. It sits below operating income with no path to a guide, so it is [sizing note removed].

evidence.text: ASIC holds $227.3m at fair value through income in Zimmer Partners-managed Utility & Infrastructure Investments ($215.9m Absolute Return Utility & Infrastructure Fund plus $11.4m MidCap LP, per the Q2 10-Q). That is about 34% of $664m book value. In Q2 those investments produced $18.6m of the $46.4m pre-tax income. In Q3 2026 the S&P 500 Utilities index fell 13.0% (vs S&P 500 +2.0%) and the 10-year yield rose from 4.30% to 5.29% (Gabelli, Oct 5). Q4 gross margin, and with it the FY guide, is at risk beyond the roughly 35% H2 GM the guide already implies.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (23 Jul): a revenue and EPS beat with a raised guide still fell 6.8%, as investors focused on an H2 EBITDA outlook below models and soft branded Americas. Q4 2025 (Feb 2026): a margin/profit miss fell 11.4%. Q1 2026: a guide raise on lower freight and tariffs rose 29.7%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Piper's 9 Sep $5M/quarter freight estimate, the BofA cut to $72 on 9 Oct and the 38% drawdown all reflect it. But every published freight number assumes 'rates held', and the stock has since bounced 24% to $62.7. If the market fully expected a Q4 guide cut, the stock would not have recovered most of the drawdown into the print and calls would not be bid. Management's own July assumption (rates fall back) is what the guide rests on, and the series says it did not happen.
evidence.independence: Drewry WCI (separate source): Shanghai-NY $9,507 on 20 Aug, https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/?p=1141388. Silk Chains 10 Sep (Xeneta, Hormuz closure since 28 Feb): https://www.silkchains.com.sg/blog/coconut-market-2026-review-q4-outlook/. Shares the oil shock with the domestic-logistics finding.

evidence.text: Coconut raw-material costs in Q3 2026 were far below a year earlier. Colombo nut auctions were 9.4% lower in LKR (about 18% in USD) than in Sep 2025. Philippine desiccated coconut averaged 135 c/lb against 174 a year ago. Copra millgate and farmgate prices were 'far below year-earlier levels', and coconut oil in August was 32% below the Q3 2025 average. These are a gross-margin offset to freight that the guide's 'cost inflation' framing does not mention.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 GM ex-refund was helped by 'lower finished goods costs' and the stock still fell 6.8%. Q1 2026 GM up on pricing and lower freight rose 29.7%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every preview and target cut found discusses freight and none discusses coconut input deflation. If it were priced, the 'H2 GM about 35%' narrative would carry an offset. This is a proxy: Vita Coco buys coconut water from co-packers, mostly from young or mature nuts not sold at these auctions, and the transmission to its finished-goods cost is unconfirmed.
evidence.independence: Silk Chains 10 Sep 2026 (Sri Lanka nuts -18% USD YoY, CNO -32% vs Q3 2025): https://www.silkchains.com.sg/blog/coconut-market-2026-review-q4-outlook/. evidence.text: Q3 is the first quarter with Copra consolidated (closed 22 Jul 2026, $175M upfront; Copra guided calendar-2026 net sales above $100M, a cold-chain business growing 48% CAGR). It adds something like $25-30M to Q3 revenue. The street revenue bar is split: Earnings Whispers has $205.9M while Investing.com and Benzinga have about $228M, so some estimates may not carry it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats are routine for COCO (Q2 26: $216M vs $206.7M; Q3 25: $182M vs $159M) and have been both bought (Q3 25 +7.2%) and sold (Q2 26 -6.8%). The revenue line does not reliably move the stock.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Copra is inside the FY guide, which the company said includes it, and the main consensus of about $228M already sits roughly 25% above Q3 2025. Only the lower estimates would show a headline beat.
evidence.independence: Copra >$100M 2026 sales, Q2 call: https://www.beveragedaily.com/Article/2026/07/24/vita-coco-acquires-copra-to-expand-into-fast-growing-super-premium-coconut-water-market/

evidence.text: On the Q2 call (23 Jul) the CFO said Vita Coco branded was 'a little behind the category last few weeks'. He guided the category to hold in the low 20s% and said the guide implies H2 top-line deceleration ex-Copra, citing distributor builds and Walmart load-in timing. Branded Americas coconut water grew only about 14% in Q2 ($137.9M vs $120.5M), the line that sold the Q2 print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: softer branded Americas despite a total beat, -6.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the company said it publicly in July. This is net of the rest of the company: private label is guided +90-100% in the US for 2026, International grew about 60% in Q2, and Copra adds. Branded Americas weakness would need to be large to dent total revenue. Kept small.
evidence.independence: Q2 8-K segment table: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001482981/000162828026049279/coco-20260630xexx991pressr.htm (same company, a different document). No Q3 scanner data found.

evidence.text: Oil shock: Brent was $105.91 on 8 Oct and US diesel hit a record $6.53/gal in September. On the Q2 call management named higher domestic logistics, packaging and supplier energy costs as later-year margin pressures. Those inputs moved further after the 23 July guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 GM said domestic logistics partly offset gains and the stock fell 6.8% on the H2 outlook.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 7 Oct -7% day was tied to the oil and yield rebound, so part of this is in the price. The stock has since retraced, which suggests the market is not carrying a full Q4 cost hit. This is macro-to-company transmission, confirmed only directionally by management in July.
evidence.independence: Management named domestic logistics on the Q2 call: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-vita-coco-tops-q2-2026-estimates-as-sales-jump-28-93CH-4809207. Shares the oil driver with the ocean-freight finding; the cost lines are separate.

evidence.why_not_priced: Likely inside the July guide, since the regime was announced around the print date. File small. If coconut water is not exempt, Q3 COGS carries a new duty on Philippine supply that no preview mentions.
evidence.independence: Bangkok Post (Thai coconut water exempt from the 12.5%): https://www.bangkokpost.com/business/general/3291215/key-thai-exports-dodge-higher-us-tariffs

evidence.text: Crowded short into a guide-sensitive print. Short interest is 14.7% of float (5.3 DTC), up 26.5% month on month. The stock has bounced 24% off an RSI-under-30 low and the chain bids calls over puts (skew -2.39). A merely in-line H2 outlook gives the squeeze mechanism room.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 +29.7% came on a guide raise; the reactions are fat-tailed (max 29.7, median 7.2).
evidence.why_not_priced: Short interest was building into the print, not covering, by the MarketBeat count. Part of the 24% bounce may already be covering, which caps this.

evidence.text: GE Aerospace (the largest engine OEM and a direct customer tier for CRS superalloys) reported Q3 on 2026-10-20, after CRS last spoke. It raised 2026 guidance across the board (op profit to $10.9-11.0B from $10.55-10.75B) and said 'material input from priority suppliers' rose double digits YoY. Total engine deliveries rose 8% and LEAP 5% in Q3 (26% YTD). This corroborates the A&D volume behind CRS's $218-222M SAO guide and the 'engine customers capacity-constrained' comment from CRS's July call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: CRS's A&D-driven beat plus raise in Oct 2025 bought about +20%. In Jul 2026 A&D sales rose 17% with an EPS beat and a new FY27 guide, and the stock fell 5.4%. The line has paid in both directions.
evidence.why_not_priced: It came out two sessions before CRS's print, and CRS still drifted to $368.8 (-2.9% over 5 days) after it. If the market had read it through, CRS would have firmed with GE rather than kept falling. The derating looks multiple-driven (target cuts, rates), not demand-driven, so counterparty demand evidence is not what the price is pricing.
evidence.independence: Proxy (counterparty, not CRS's own number). Same direction: Boeing Q3 deliveries of 161 jets with 124 737s (https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-10-13-Boeing-Announces-Third-Quarter-Deliveries) and an Argus 2026-08-03 report that engine OEMs significantly raised H1 deliveries, lifting melter demand.

evidence.text: RTX Q3 2026 (8-K, Oct 2026): Pratt & Whitney commercial OE sales fell 5% YoY, while commercial aftermarket rose 21% (GTF) and total P&W sales rose 10%. That is a mixed read for engine OE alloy pull, the second engine OEM after GE.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No CRS-specific history of reacting to P&W OE; CRS reports A&D as one line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public days before the print and small. It matters only as an offset to the GE read, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: None from a different source. Partly offsets the GE finding; spares and aftermarket demand also consume CRS alloys, so the net is near zero.

evidence.text: Boeing delivered 161 commercial jets in Q3 2026 (124 737s, 22 787s), 475 YTD (release 2026-10-13). On the July call CRS's CEO said 'some structural customers remain cautious in their ordering patterns' and that recovery depends on Boeing's ramp. A strong delivery quarter supports the structural and fastener orders CRS flagged as ramping.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable from the overall A&D line in CRS's history.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public on Oct 13, and CRS fell after it. A secondary source says Boeing's CEO acknowledged in September that stabilising at 47/month is taking longer, which caps this. Sized small as a proxy.
evidence.independence: Secondary summary https://migflug.com/afterburner/?p=27994844 (rate 42/month, 47 delayed) cuts partly against it. GE finding above is a different document pointing the same way on engines.

evidence.text: The Q1 FY27 guide of $195-200M operating income (reduced by elevated Q1 preventative maintenance) implies EPS of about $3.08-3.12, using Q4's $206.9M operating income to $3.23 EPS and ~49.6M shares after buybacks. That sits slightly above the $3.00-3.04 consensus. Track record: Q4 FY26 landed at $206.9M inside a $205-210M guide; Q1 FY26 beat the $2.13 consensus at $2.43.

Revenue has missed consensus on the last two prints, so the EPS line alone has not been paid reliably.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it sits inside what the company told the market to expect, so it is sized near zero. Consensus below the guide midpoint suggests the street haircut the guide for maintenance and leaves a small beat cushion.
evidence.independence: Shares a document with the LTA finding (the July call). Q4 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000017843/000001784326000030/a4thqtr2026resultspressrel.htm gives the Q4 base.

evidence.text: On the July 30 call CEO Thene said a large LTA renewal is under negotiation, that other significant contracts come up over the next two years, and that price will be 'a big driver' in FY27. He also said 'if investors treat [the $850-880M FY27 guide] as the floor, you wouldn't get any pushback from me.' The Q1 call is the first chance to announce the renewal or raise or firm the FY27 range.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY26: the initial $660-700M guide (Oct 2025) was raised over the year to $700-705M and landed at $702M. The Oct 2025 print with the guide came with +20%. The July 2026 FY27 guide plus a FY29 $1.2-1.3B target came with -5.4% (a CEO death the same week confounds it).

The market is applying a lower multiple and is not visibly paying for a guide raise or LTA pricing. If it were, the stock would not be -35% since the guide was given. Whether the renewal lands in this window is uncertain, hence the wide band.

evidence.text: The stock has de-rated about 40% from its $625.99 high (spot $368.8) and about 35% since the July print. Sell-side cut targets sharply in October (JPM 700 to 520 on 10-14, TD Cowen 650 to 500 on 10-09, KeyBanc 608 to 465 on 10-08, Wells Fargo to 430) but kept positive ratings. Ortex describes these as valuation revisions ('what that business is worth at current market conditions') with no fundamental cut. Short interest is ~3% of float, about 2.6 days to cover.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Oct 2025 print after a quieter tape: +20%. July 2026 print after a run to highs: -5.4%. A low bar after a drawdown has preceded the larger positive reaction on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Expectations have reset on the multiple, not the numbers, so a print at or above the guide is measured against a de-rated price. The +4.3 skew argues the option market still pays for downside. Reasons it may be wrong for this print: the chain is thin (OI 1,779, 19% spread), and peer HWM's derating came from a GE-in-sourcing scare (GE buying CPP castings, Sep 2026) rather than from demand. Sized small for being against the skew.
evidence.independence: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/crs/ lists the same target cuts. Sector context: HWM fell ~11% on GE's CPP purchase (https://www.tikr.com/de/blog/howmet-aerospace-stock-dropped-nearly-11-after-ge-bought-a-rival-casting-supplier-heres-whether-the-selloff-is-an-overreaction).

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior tax one-off on this name in the baseline. On Q2 (2026-07-22) a GAAP EPS miss ($0.23 vs $0.34-0.355) driven by provisions brought +2.45% close to close. Holders looked through below-the-line items in the headline.

evidence.text: The FY2026 guide of 'mid-single-digit annual EBITDA growth over 2025' ($562.8M) requires an H2 ramp that the reported numbers make steep. evidence.text: Q3 revenue consensus ($16.84-16.85bn) sits above IBM's own stated base case for the quarter. On the Q2 call (2026-07-22) management guided Q3 constant-currency growth 'consistent with the full year' (4-5%, low end the base case) with FX a 1.5pt headwind. On the Q3 2025 base of $16.33bn that gives about $16.74bn at the low end and $16.90bn at the high. The Street is therefore pricing roughly the upper half of the guide, on a company that missed revenue by about $0.66bn last quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue miss ($17.16bn vs ~$17.5-17.9bn): -25.2% on the pre-announcement (2026-07-14), then +0.43% on the full print. Q1 2026 beat: -8.25%. Q3 2025 beat ($16.33bn, +9%): -0.87%. IBM has repeatedly sold revenue beats.
evidence.why_not_priced: The guide is public, but the consensus sits about $0.1bn above the low end that management called its base case. If the market had marked to the base case, revenue estimates would read about $16.74bn rather than $16.84bn. Evercore expects 'in line to slightly better', which shows the Street is anchored above the low end.
evidence.independence: Q3 2025 revenue base from https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/ibm-q2-2026-earnings. Consensus from Zacks and Benzinga via https://finviz.com/news/399932/ibm-to-announce-third-quarter-2026-financial-results. UBS's $16.68bn estimate (cited at https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262220955-ibm-stock-forecast-q3-earnings-deal-recovery-238-breakout-october-16-2026-tradingkey) points the same way. This finding shares the transcript with the slipped-deals finding below.

evidence.text: The driver IBM blamed for the Q2 software and ELA deferrals did not stop in Q3. TrendForce (2026-07-03) forecast conventional DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ in 3Q26, with server DRAM still undersupplied, though rising more slowly than in prior quarters. IBM said the low end of its 6-8% FY software range 'assumes that recent spending dynamics persist through the second half', so this proxy points to the low end of the software range in Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-07-14 pre-announcement, which attributed the miss to client capex shifting to servers, storage and memory: -25.2%. The full Q2 print a week later: +0.43%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced, since the memory story is well known. But the Street's focus, per Evercore, is on deferral 'rather than destruction' and on slipped deals converting in Q3. Continued price increases mean the incentive to pull budget toward hardware persisted through the quarter. If this were priced, the consensus would sit at the guide's low end.
evidence.independence: Proxy only; neither IBM nor a direct counterparty has confirmed it for Q3. The moderation in price increases (https://www.igorslab.de/en/dram-and-nand-remain-more-expensive-trendforce-sees-slowing-but-still-rising-memory-prices-q3-2026/) cuts the other way, which is why the size is small. The offset elsewhere in the company: IBM Distributed Infrastructure (Power and Storage, +37% in Q2 with a ~$500M backlog) benefits from the same shift.

evidence.text: Slipped-deal recapture is on company record. On the Q2 call Krishna said 'about a third' of the large deals that slipped from Q2 closed in the first few weeks of Q3, and that he would normally expect 'two-thirds to three-quarters of them to close over the next six months'. That transactional software revenue should land in Q3, against a quarter the company guided only to the FY growth rate.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The full Q2 print carrying this commentary rose +0.43% after the -25% pre-announcement, so the market gave it little credit.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public since July and mostly priced. UBS reads the recapture as 'less than half', and the Street still sits inside the guide rather than above it. If the market believed the recapture plus normal Q3 flow, Q3 software estimates would be above the 6-8% FY run-rate. What is left unpriced is whether the remaining two-thirds also closed by September.
evidence.independence: Fox Business interview, 2026-07-23 (https://www.foxbusiness.com/media/ibm-ceo-addresses-wall-street-tech-panic-after-delayed-enterprise-software-deals-surge-back): same claim, same speaker, so not independent. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-22): record quarter, FY EBITDA guide raised to +45-55%, stock +9.91%. Q1 2026 (2026-04-22): record quarter and raised outlook, +1.11%. Q3 2025: big beat (adj EPS $1.86 vs ~$0.89), +19.54%. Q4 2025 (no numeric guide): -8.85%.

evidence.independence: Q1 2026 results ($129M EBITDA, $36M lag) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000811596/000119312526170615/kalu-ex99_1.htm and FY2025 release ($310M) https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260218643721/en/Kaiser-Aluminum-Corporation-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results; all company documents, so this is one arithmetic on company numbers. Partly shares the metal-price premise with finding 2. Counter: the CFO said H2 carries heavier maintenance and fewer shipping days (finding 5), which is part of why the guide is low.

evidence.text: Q3 2026 metal prices rose through the quarter relative to the cost basis Kaiser carried out of Q2: the CFO said exiting Q2 its weighted-average metal inventory cost matched the forward Midwest Transaction Price of $2.45/lb, while LME cash went from ~$3,073/t on 1 July to ~$3,250-3,325/t in September and the Midwest premium held ~$1.10-1.11/lb (Fastmarkets 110-112c on 7 July, Platts 109.7c on 10 Sept), putting the Midwest Transaction Price near $2.50/lb in July and ~$2.57/lb in September; that points to neutral-to-favourable Q3 metal lag against a guide and consensus built on neutral, partly offset by Alcoa's average realized price falling 4.7% q/q (lower average pass-through, mostly a net-sales effect).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Metal lag drove the last two beats: Q1 2026 ~$36M favourable lag (+1.11%), Q2 2026 ~$27M (+9.91%); FY2025 ~$93M of favourable lag.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of ~$2.1-2.2 is consistent with zero lag; Kaiser does not disclose lag until the print and sell-side models tend to assume the company's neutral guidance, so a positive lag line would show up as an EPS beat. If priced, consensus would have drifted up through September and the stock would not have fallen 22% off its high.
evidence.independence: Proxy, not company-confirmed. LME path: https://www.alcircle.com/news/lme-aluminium-price-chart-rises-further-to-3-325-t-stocks-remain-stable-121104 and https://www.alcircle.com/news/lme-aluminium-price-drops-nearly-1-stocks-hold-firm-at-241-375t-on-september-30-121365 ; MWP: https://www.fastmarkets.com/insights/correction-to-rationale-of-daily-aluminium-p1020a-premium-ddp-midwest-us/ and https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/metals/091126-us-tariff-cut-on-canadian-aluminum-wont-lower-midwest-premium-by-much-alcoa ; counterweight Alcoa realized price -4.7% q/q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001675149/000119312526422891/aa-ex99_1.htm. evidence.text: Crown Holdings reported on 2026-10-19 that North American beverage can shipments rose 6% in Q3 2026 (vs +5% in Q2 and a 3-4% full-year regional guide), and that October shipments were stronger, a direct-customer-class read for Kaiser's Warrick can-sheet volumes (packaging is ~half of Kaiser's pounds; Q2 packaging shipments +10.4%).

KNX's own Q3 consensus is still $0.75, the midpoint of its $0.71-0.77 guide, and KNX has not pre-announced.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: KNX sold a large Q2 beat on 2026-07-22 (adj EPS $0.63 against $0.49 consensus and a $0.45-0.49 guide, with the Q3 guide above consensus): -4.88%. On 2025-10-22 it fell -7.13%. Its reported-quarter surprises have not been paid; the guide drives the move.
evidence.why_not_priced: KNX's sell-side bar has not absorbed it: Zacks' consensus of $0.75 was down only 1.3% in 60 days as of Oct 15, before Werner spoke. If the market had fully transmitted Werner's 55% miss to KNX, KNX would have fallen on Oct 19-20 and its consensus would sit near the bottom of the guide. Instead KNX is +0.65% over 5 days. Partly priced: WERN itself fell only 1.1% on the warning (it was already 31% off its mid-July peak), and KNX is 23% off its high.
evidence.independence: JBHT warned in mid-September of a 5-10% q/q earnings decline on diesel near $6.30 and $25m of added driver costs (https://www.xtb.com/en/market-analysis/jb-hunt-shares-down-13-us-transportation-stocks-have-problems); that is a separate document and is filed as its own finding. evidence.text: JBHT's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-15): truckload revenue per load rose 29% and segment revenue 37%, yet truckload operating income fell 6% and DCS operating income fell 22%, on purchased transportation, driver pay, insurance and fuel costs. Fuel expense rose to 7.1% of revenue from 5.4%. The CFO said rapid fuel moves 'create a timing mismatch and dilute margins'. Q3 EPS was down 5% q/q, at the better end of the September warning.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: As above: KNX sold its last beat (-4.88%) and fell -7.13% in Oct 2025. JBHT itself traded -2.3% after hours on its print, after a -13% day on the September warning.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public and widely read, so it is mostly priced. KNX's consensus at the guide midpoint shows the sell side has not carried that across.
evidence.independence: Werner's pre-announcement (separate company, separate document) names the same three cost lines. CFO quote: https://talkbusiness.net/2026/10/j-b-hunt-third-quarter-earnings-rise-narrowly-revenue-up-20/

evidence.text: Truckload conditions eased during Q3 after the July 22 guide, which assumed 'current conditions continue with pressured capacity'. SONAR tender rejections fell from a cycle peak above 17.5% around July 4 to about 13.5% at Labor Day. DAT recorded the steepest July-to-August spot decline in its 16-year history, and spot fell below contract by August. September spot linehaul ex-fuel slipped again (van $2.17, -2c m/m) while contract linehaul held ($2.40, -1c). KNX's true spot exposure is in the low-to-mid teens percent of its truckload book.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's rapid tightening produced a beat that was sold (-4.88%). No case on file of an easing intra-quarter spot market moving KNX.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is an industry proxy, not a KNX number, and is mostly priced. The residual is that a guide set at the July spot peak embedded spot-exposed revenue that August and September did not deliver. Lower spot also cuts purchased-transportation cost in KNX's Logistics segment (Q2 Logistics OR 96.4% on high purchased-transportation cost), so the net effect is small.
evidence.independence: Tender-rejection path: https://www.freightwaves.com/?p=583148 (2026-10-14). Spot exposure 'low-to-mid teens': https://www.freightwaves.com/?p=572459 (2026-04-23).

evidence.text: The SONAR Truckload Rejection Index jumped to 14.17% in mid-October 2026 (FreightWaves, 2026-10-14). That is about three times the 2023-2025 range, comes on a supply shortfall with flat tender volume, and has spot above contract on 38% of the top-50 Los Angeles lanes. It bears on the Q4 guide KNX gives tonight, against a Q4 EPS consensus of about $0.81 that is above the Q3 bar and already assumes further contract repricing.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Jul 2026 a Q3 guide above consensus came with -4.88% (on top of a large beat). In Apr 2026 the Q2 guide was reiterated after a Q1 miss and the stock rose +2.8%. In Jan 2026 the Q4 2025 print with a capacity-tightening narrative went +2.61%. The guide line has paid in both directions.
evidence.why_not_priced: SONAR is widely watched, but the stock has fallen 5.3% in 20 days and broke its 200-day average on Oct 9, i.e. it traded the peer cost warnings and not the October re-tightening. If the market had priced a strong Q4 guide, KNX would not sit 23% off its high with consensus Q3 unchanged. The skew (-3.23, upside paid) and the call-heavy open interest lean the same way, so this agrees with the options and is partly in them.
evidence.independence: Schneider's Q2 2026 call described a driver-constrained market, spot testing prior-cycle highs, double-digit renewals and early-stage contract recovery (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/schneider-national-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-31/). evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 fuel and weather cost 5-6c and the stock still rose +2.8% on the reiterated guide; Q2 net fuel was positive and the beat was sold. Fuel has not been a line this stock trades on.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Werner and JBHT read-through treats rising fuel as a uniform carrier headwind. KNX's own filing shows the surcharge out-recovering fuel cost in Q2. If the market had absorbed that, KNX would have decoupled from WERN's 31% drawdown; it is 23% off its high instead. However, Q3's rise was steeper (Aug +10%, Sept +15% retail; one-week surcharge lag), so the Q2 surplus may not repeat, hence the small size.
evidence.independence: ODFL August update (https://www.ajot.com/news/old-dominion-freight-line-provides-update-for-third-quarter-2026), showing the LTL fuel-surcharge mechanism. The monthly diesel path cuts the other way (https://www.freightwaves.com/?p=583491).

first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is about 2.3% of float, down from 2.5% in early September (Benzinga sentiment snapshot of 2026-09-25, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LRCX/sentiment). evidence.text: Customers and peers that spoke after Lam's 29 July call all point to a December-quarter equipment step-up, which supports a December guide above the $8.52B sell-side average. TSMC (15 Oct) kept 2026 capex at $60-64B after spending $13.8B in Q3, so Q4 needs $19.4-23.4B (+40-70% q/q), and it said 2026-28 capex will be 'significantly higher'. ASML (14 Oct) guided Q4 sales to EUR 14.2-15.2B from EUR 11.7B in Q3 and said 2027-28 supply will not meet demand. Samsung's Q3 operating profit was a record KRW 107.4T, with memory around KRW 110T. Micron (30 Sep) raised capex, with first-half FY27 near $25B. The market expects a December guide of about $8.5B (sell-side), against a Morgan Stanley case for more than $9B.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is the line Lam trades on. On 2026-07-29 a September guide about 14% above consensus ($8.1B vs ~$7.11B) bought +17.98% close to close (baseline; https://www.tradingpedia.com/2026/07/30/lam-research-soars-after-record-results-and-strong-outlook/). Five of the last seven prints were up, with a median absolute move of 4.45%.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the stock had priced the counterparties' acceleration it would not have fallen 24% in ten sessions straight through TSMC's and ASML's prints; equipment lagged the chipmakers' rebound on 20 Oct. The published December consensus of $8.52B is only about +5% q/q, below what TSMC's implied Q4 capex step and Morgan Stanley's >$9B case suggest. Against that, sell-side previews (MS, UBS 'even more robust guidance') are public, so part of this is the whisper, and the finding is a customer proxy, not Lam's own number.
evidence.independence: Several independent counterparties. ASML Q4 guide and supply commentary: https://investinglive.com/stocks/asml-says-2027-and-2028-supply-will-fall-short-of-demand-as-q3-sales-hit-a-record/ (2026-10-14). Samsung Q3 preliminary: https://news.samsung.com/global/samsung-electronics-announces-earnings-guidance-for-third-quarter-2026 (2026-10-08). Micron capex: https://www.mobileworldlive.com/ai-cloud/micron-ramps-capex-to-address-shortage/ (Sep 2026). Morgan Stanley expects the WFE run-rate above $200B (+60% y/y) in the December quarter (tradingview link in bar).

evidence.text: The December-quarter bar is higher than the printed consensus. The sell-side average is $8.52B (high $9B), while Morgan Stanley (Oct 5, PT $385) says it would not rule out a guide above $9B, citing DRAM and 2nm pull-ins, and UBS expects 'even more robust guidance'. A guide in the $8.6-8.9B band would 'beat consensus' and could still disappoint the buy-side number.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-04-22 Lam fell 2.63% after its print. The baseline does not say on which line; I found no source tying that fall to the guide, so I record only the move.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sell-side average in data feeds ($8.52B) is not the number holders will judge the guide against. If the higher bar were fully reflected in the $8.52B, Yahoo's high and average would be close together. The 24% drawdown partly lowers this whisper, which is why the finding is small.
evidence.independence: UBS 'very strong report and even more robust guidance', via https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/lam-research-stock-falls-nine-straight-sessions-down-21-7/53639693 (2026-10-16). It shares the MS note with finding 1's bar context: two readings of one bar, but opposite in effect (finding 1 is the fundamental, this is the hurdle).

evidence.text: Positioning was washed out into the print with no company-specific cause. Lam had ten straight down sessions to $263.94 on 16 Oct (-24%, about $104B of market value, the longest losing streak since its 1984 listing). The trigger was Applied Materials declining to give a WFE forecast at its 13 Oct investor day, plus profit-taking. Equipment names kept lagging chipmakers on 20 Oct, and spot is $267.89, 38% below the June high, on about 34x forward earnings.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July print came after a 10% one-day drop on 2 July on 'AI capex peak' fears, with the stock at $252 into the print, and it rallied +17.98%. That is one prior case of a washed-out setup followed by a strong guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: The drawdown is itself the price. The question is whether the reaction to a good guide is asymmetric. Skew is only +3 vol pts, so the option market is not pricing a skewed downside after a 24% fall. If holders were still crowded long, I would expect a steeper put skew and the stock holding up with chips on 20 Oct, and it did not.
evidence.independence: Applied Materials investor-day trigger: https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/2675610673. Equipment lagging chips on 20 Oct: https://www.aol.com/articles/chip-stocks-shrug-off-scary-154222000.html (2026-10-20). Profit-taking with fundamentals intact: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/19/lam-research-imploded-by-20-in-the-last-3-months-this-respected-wall-street-firm-says-its-about-to-double/ (2026-10-19).

evidence.text: The September quarter is likely at or above the guide midpoint: consensus is $8.13B / $2.18 against a $8.1B +/- $0.4B / $2.15 guide, and Lam has beaten EPS five quarters in a row. This lands inside what the company already guided.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: June quarter: revenue $6.72B and record EPS $1.82 beat. The reaction was driven by the guide, not the quarter.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Consensus sits on the guide midpoint, so a beat toward the top of the range is the usual pattern and small.
evidence.independence: Five straight EPS beats: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/19/lam-research-imploded-by-20-in-the-last-3-months-this-respected-wall-street-firm-says-its-about-to-double/

evidence.text: China is the open risk to the December guide and to the commentary. China fell to 26% of revenue in the June quarter from 34%. The BIS Affiliates (50%) rule suspension was due to lapse on 10 Nov 2026; Bessent extended the trade truce to 10 Jan 2027 (23 Sep), but whether the Affiliates rule stays suspended is reported as unresolved.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In the July print China dropped from 34% to 26% of revenue and the stock still rose 18%, so a falling China mix has been absorbed when the rest grows.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced and known. What is not known is how management frames China in the December guide around a rule whose status is unresolved; a cautious China comment would pull the guide toward the sell-side number. Netted against the rest of the company: non-China (memory, leading-edge logic) is about 74% of revenue and accelerating per finding 1, so the net size is small.
evidence.independence: Affiliates rule unresolved: https://www.bkl.co.kr/en/law/insight/newsletter/6811. China mix 34% to 26%: Hudson Labs preview (finding 4's source).

evidence.text: BIS Affiliates rule suspension nominally lapses on 10 Nov 2026 unless extended; the trade truce runs to 10 Jan 2027. A re-imposition would hit Lam's China revenue.

first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 24.54m shares, 5.06% of float, 3.5 days to cover, record date 2026-09-30, up 11.2% from 22.08m on 2026-09-15 (MarketBeat from FINRA, published 2026-10-09: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/LUV/short-interest/). Not a crowded short. Baseline: 25-delta skew +3.7 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.58, event-implied move 5.15%, straddle 5.48%. Spot $40.78 is +3.66% over 5 days, -0.63% over 20 days and 25.6% below the 52-week high; it rose about 2.7% on 2026-10-21 after UAL's print. Reaction history: 5 of the last 7 prints were down; the last two amc prints with guide cuts or no guide update were -6.19% and -4.07%; one +18.7% in Jan 2026. Same-window co-event: American Airlines reports Q3 before the open on 2026-10-22, inside LUV's window.

evidence.text: Q3 fuel very likely ran above Southwest's $3.70-3.75/gal guide assumption, which rested on the 17 July curve. Peers that reported after LUV last spoke came in over their own July assumptions by about $0.20: Alaska $3.94 against $3.75, United $3.90 against $3.69. On roughly 580m gallons a quarter (derived from the $889m Q2 y/y fuel increase), $0.20/gal is about $115m pre-tax, or about $0.17 of EPS before any fare recapture (UAL recaptured 72%). Net of recapture that is about $0.05-0.09 below the $0.625 guide midpoint, roughly onto the $0.57 consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 fuel came in below guide ($3.92 against $4.10-4.15) and adj EPS beat at $0.94 against about $0.51, yet the stock fell -6.19% on the FY guide cut. LUV has not paid for reported-quarter EPS surprises recently.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Q3 consensus is $0.57, below the $0.625 guide midpoint, after 16 down and 2 up revisions and a 3.4% drift down over 30 days. If the full fuel overrun were unpriced, consensus would still sit at or above the midpoint. What may remain is a residual of a few cents if Southwest's leisure-heavy domestic network recaptured less fuel through fares than UAL's.
evidence.independence: UAL Q3 fuel of $3.90 against a $3.69 July assumption (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ual-q3-earnings-miss-surging-121000795.html; July assumption at https://www.tikr.com/blog/united-airlines-guided-q3-below-the-street-the-fuel-price-behind-it-came-from-one-days-curve). Delta absorbed more than $500m of fuel above its early-July guide (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx). LUV's assumption is from its Q2 8-K.

evidence.text: The Q4 guide and the FY cut will be set at a much higher fuel price than anything Southwest has guided on. Peers' Q4 all-in assumptions are $4.65-4.85 (ALK, 20 Oct, which guides a Q4 loss of $2.00-2.50/share), about $4.80 (UAL, against Q3's $3.90) and about $4.25 (DAL on 9 Oct, before Brent reached $110 on 19 Oct). Southwest is unhedged after terminating its contracts. FY consensus of $2.88 already sits below the $3.25-4.25 guided floor, so the cut itself is expected. The open question is how far the Q4 guide falls below a consensus that is itself unsourced: about $0.9 is only implied by FY $2.88 less Q1 $0.45, Q2 $0.94 and Q3 $0.57. Each extra $0.50/gal on about 580m gallons is roughly $0.45/share.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is what moves LUV. Jul 2026: FY cut from at least $4.00 to $3.25-4.25 on a large beat, -6.19%. Apr 2026: declined to update the $4.00 FY guide, -4.07%. Jan 2026: the new-model guide drove +18.7%. Peers this month: DAL fell about 3% on its FY cut (9 Oct); UAL rose about 4.8% after hours on a Q4 midpoint of $1.00 against $1.88 consensus (20 Oct).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. FY consensus is already below the guide floor, Brent at $110 is public, put skew is +3.7, and LUV trades 25.6% below its 52-week high. What could be unpriced is the Q4 number: peers' consensus was stale by 40-50% on Q4 (UAL $1.00 midpoint against $1.88). If LUV's Q4 consensus has not caught up, the guide lands far below it. If the market had fully priced this, LUV would not have rallied 3.7% over 5 days into the print.
evidence.independence: UAL Q4 fuel of $4.80 and guide of $0.50-1.50 against $1.75-1.88 consensus (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/united-airlines-falls-on-weak-fourth-quarter-guidance-4960956; https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ual-q3-earnings-miss-surging-121000795.html). Delta Q4 fuel of $4.25 and guide of $1.15-1.65 against $1.86 a year earlier (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx). Wholesale jet fuel of about $4.95/gal in NY on 10 Oct (Bloomberg via search snippet, https://www.globalair.com/articles/aviation-fuel-spotlight-oil-is-flowing-but-jet-a-didnt-get-the-memo/12728, snippet_only). Brent reached $110 on 19 Oct (247wallst, 2026-10-21). The FY consensus figure shares the 247wallst document with the bar.

evidence.text: The sector's reaction function this week has been to buy fuel-driven guide-downs when demand holds. United guided Q4 EPS to $0.50-1.50 against about $1.88 consensus, said it is 'highly confident' of recapturing 100% of fuel with a lag, and saw sell-in yields up high-teens. Its shares rose about 4.8% after hours on 20 Oct (to $102.51 from $97.77) and were up again on 21 Oct. LUV rose about 2.7% intraday on 21 Oct in sympathy (24/7 Wall St widget, $39.55 to $40.74; baseline spot $40.78).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line cuts against LUV's own history: its last two guide cuts were sold (-6.19%, -4.07%). Among peers this month, DAL's cut was sold about 3% (9 Oct) and UAL's was bought about 5% (20-21 Oct). ALK's reaction to its 20 Oct loss guide was not found.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: LUV has already rallied about 3.7% over 5 days, most of it on 21 Oct. The UAL template suggests investors are anchored on recapture with a lag rather than on Q4 EPS, so a Q4 guide far below a stale consensus may not be sold as hard as the July cut was. If this were fully in the price, the skew would have flattened from +3.7.
evidence.independence: Same UAL event as the price data in https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/united-airlines-falls-on-weak-fourth-quarter-guidance-4960956 (shares up in early trading 21 Oct). TD Cowen called UAL's consensus 'irrelevant' and weakness a buying opportunity (same article). Counter-case: DAL's 9 Oct cut was sold about 3% (rttnews).

evidence.text: Network carriers are adding domestic seats into Q4: an analyst on UAL's Q3 call said United and American each plan roughly 8-9% domestic capacity growth in Q4. That is pressure on Southwest's all-domestic RASM just as it needs fares to recapture fuel. UAL's CEO separately expects 6-10 US airlines to lose money this year and 'supply changes' if oil stays high.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No LUV-specific history on competitor capacity commentary found. In 2024-25 LUV's RASM guides were cut on domestic capacity glut episodes, but no source was retrieved here, so treat that as context only.
evidence.why_not_priced: Schedule data is public to airline analysts, so this is likely mostly priced. It reaches LUV's guide only if management cites competitive pressure in the Q4 RASM range. If it were unpriced, LUV would have lagged UAL on 21 Oct, and it did not.
evidence.independence: A proxy: an analyst's statement on another airline's call, not confirmed by Southwest. Shares the UAL transcript document with the positioning finding.

evidence.text: Peer unit revenue in Q3 was strong and above guides, which supports Southwest landing at or above the top of its +17.5-19.5% RASM guide. ALK RASM was +11.7% against 'low double digits' guided, with September yield up about 17%. UAL TRASM was +15.9% (best since the pandemic) and domestic PRASM +14.5%. DAL domestic unit revenue was +16%. LUV's comparison also gets assigned seating (live from 27 Jan 2026, so a y/y benefit through Q4), and Spirit's exit on 2 May 2026 removed about 21.3m seats May-Dec, concentrated at FLL, MCO, LAS and HOU, which are Southwest-heavy airports.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: adj RASM +20.1%, above guide, yet the stock fell -6.19% because the guide set the move. A RASM beat inside the guided band has not paid on its own.
evidence.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus of $8.24B (+18.6%) already sits near the guide midpoint, so a top-of-range RASM is worth about +0.5% on revenue. The value is mainly what it implies for Q4 fare recapture: the Q4 RASM guide would be visibly higher than a +18% repeat. Spirit's exit is five months old and priced.
evidence.independence: UAL (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ual-q3-earnings-miss-surging-121000795.html); DAL (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx); Spirit shutdown 2 May 2026 (https://katv.com/news/nation-world/spirit-shutdown-fl-based-budget-airline-ceases-operations-after-failed-federal-buyout). All are peer proxies; Southwest has given no Q3 RASM update since July.

evidence.text: The buyback has stopped. Southwest repurchased nothing in Q2 2026, against $1.5B in Q2 2025, after $1.25B in H1, and only $450m remains on the $2.0B authorization. With an unhedged fuel bill rising in Q4, a restart announced with the print is unlikely, so per-share support from repurchases is gone for now.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolable. The Sept 2024 $2.5B buyback announcement was a positive catalyst, but it came outside a print.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it was disclosed in July. It matters only if the release confirms no Q3 repurchases or withdraws the remaining authorization.
evidence.independence: none

evidence.text: The August 2026 8-Ks show a new $2B five-year revolver (accordion to $3B, undrawn, replacing a 2016 facility, 10 Aug), two new directors, and executive pay raised to peer levels citing 'heightened risk of losing key senior executive talent'. Liquidity was $5.3B at Q2 with gross leverage 2.1x.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; no print-day effect expected.
evidence.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: an undrawn standby facility replacing an old one, which is routine liquidity backup and not distress. With fuel elevated it is a mild comfort rather than a negative. It has been public since August.
evidence.independence: Aggregator summaries of the 8-Ks (https://www.boardroomalpha.com/sec/luv-8-k-2026-08-12-0000092380-26-000098).

evidence.text: UAL management expects fuel to stay elevated through 2027 and that 2027 industry capacity plans are not firm; supply cuts by loss-making carriers would be a medium-term tailwind for Southwest's domestic yields.

If fully priced the stock would not have drifted -4% in five sessions into the print; what is not priced is only the residual if revenue prints above $64B, the top of the guide.
evidence.independence: Same direction from BofA estimate in https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-meta-platforms-stock-sliding-today-93CH-4957820 (2026-10-19) and the Bernstein/DB summary at https://www.tipranks.com/news/meta-q3-earnings-preview-what-bernstein-expects-from-meta-stock; all sell-side, not independent of each other.

evidence.text: Tonight is the first look at 2027 spend: Meta has given no 2027 capex number; previews put 2027 capex consensus at ~$193B (BofA $205B, Evercore ~+$70B YoY i.e. ~$200B+ on a $130-145B 2026 guide), Evercore's Mahaney expects capex and total expense targets ABOVE consensus and a cut to 2027 profit estimates, Morgan Stanley models D&A rising from ~$31.5B (2026) to ~$59B (2027), and Q2 free cash flow was only $784M.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The analogous call a year ago (Q3-25, 2025-10-29), when Meta said 2026 capex would be 'notably larger' and expenses would grow 'significantly faster', produced -11.33%; Q2-26 (raised expense guide) -7.95%; Q1-26 -8.55%. Forward-spend framing has been the line this stock trades on.
evidence.why_not_priced: The consensus capex bar (~$193B) is below what two banks model ($200-205B), so a guide in line with those banks would still read as above consensus. If the market had fully absorbed a $200B+ number, the skew would lean to puts and the stock would not sit only 9% off its high after a 27% September rally; instead skew is -2 (calls bid). Capped because the capex bar is single-source.
evidence.independence: Evercore/BofA 2027 EPS-pressure view also reported at https://finance.biggo.com/news/7704261d-f24f-48c4-b5be-014986e460d6 and BofA's warning on 2027 EPS in the TipRanks piece above; the reaction history is from the sealed baseline.

evidence.text: Q3 GAAP results will carry an ~$10B legal accrual for the 29-state youth-harm settlement (up to ~$18B over 10 years, ~$12.7B unconditional), which Meta said on 2026-08-26 is outside its $165-169B expense guide; GAAP EPS estimates in the wire range from $3.79 (BofA, charge included) to $6.54-$7.54 (charge excluded), so headline 'EPS miss' prints are likely on aggregator screens.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2-26 $2.4B legal charge plus $1.18B severance made a GAAP EPS miss ($6.18 vs ~$7.2) and the stock fell 7.95%, though the guide was the stated driver. The settlement announcement itself on 2026-08-26 lifted the stock ~4.4% pre-market (overhang removed).
evidence.why_not_priced: The charge itself is public for two months and is priced; what may not be is the mechanical headline-EPS reaction in the first minutes because consensus aggregators mix pre- and post-charge estimates. Cash is spread over 10 years, so no path to the multiple; sized as a fraction.
evidence.independence: Charge size confirmed in https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262225065-meta-stock-forecast-q3-earnings-legal-charge-capex-694-support-october-20-2026-tradingkey (2026-10-20) and EPS dispersion in the cmsinvestments preview; same underlying Meta statement.

evidence.text: The same settlement imposes a 2-hour cumulative daily limit on Facebook+Instagram for under-18s, a midnight-6am night mode and an 8am-3pm school mode in participating states, pending judicial approval with no effective date; any engagement or Q4/2027 revenue commentary on it lands tonight.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print on this line; the August settlement day was positive (+4.4% pre-market), so the market has so far treated the restrictions as small.
evidence.why_not_priced: No company quantification exists; if the market thought teen limits material, the August reaction would not have been positive. Teen users are a small share of ad revenue, so the residual is small and one-directional.
evidence.independence: Shares the settlement document with the legal-charge finding (one document, two lines: the accrual and the product restriction). Restrictions also described at https://6abc.com/post/meta-settles-states-landmark-social-media-addiction-trial/19738688/.

evidence.why_not_priced: Financing question answered: the commitments buy compute capacity for Meta's own demand, not to fund distress, and Meta held $90.3B cash vs $83.7B LTD at Q2; so this is a narrative/credit-contagion risk, not a balance-sheet problem. evidence.text: Elevance, Molina's largest listed Medicaid peer, reported Q3 2026 this morning (2026-10-21). Its Medicaid results beat its own outlook 'mainly from recent rate actions'. The CFO said the July 1 updates 'did provide greater support to the second half margins', full-year Medicaid margin is now 'slightly ahead' of guidance, and cost trend is 'elevated but broadly stable and consistent with Q2'. Molina's 2H guide assumed a ~1.9% ex-Florida Medicaid pre-tax margin with no rate increases and 5% trend, and a full-year 4% rate vs 5% trend, so similar mid-year rate actions in Molina's states would land above its guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Medicaid MCR is the line Molina trades on (100 bp of Medicaid MCR is about $5/share per the Q2 call). Q1 2026's beat on cost control bought +14.2%. Q2 2026's beat with an unchanged 92.9% Medicaid MCR guide fell 9.7% because Marketplace was cut. Q3 2025 (-17.5%) and Q4 2025 (-25.5%) both fell on Medicaid and Marketplace cost resets.
evidence.why_not_priced: Elevance printed about 9 hours before Molina, after every estimate in the bar was set. If the market had read it as a Medicaid read-through, MOH would be up today. Instead it slid from $219.72 (10:32 ET, Investing.com) to $215.1 at the 17:10 UTC seal, tracking ELV's ~2% drop on the quality of its non-operating beat. The read-through on the Medicaid line looks to have been sold with ELV's headline rather than priced into MOH. Molina is ~90% Medicaid by premium, so the line matters far more to it than to ELV.
evidence.independence: Partly shares a document with the Elevance ACA finding (same call), but a different line. UNH Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000731766/000073176626000255/earningsrelease3q26unh.htm) shows the consolidated MCR improving but gives no Medicaid margin. Molina's own Q2 call said off-cycle rate increases so far were 'small and within expectations', which caps this finding.

evidence.text: Elevance's Individual ACA business is 'tracking ahead of full-year expectations with a modestly higher margin'. Claims are developing favorably, the seasonal bronze cost ramp is arriving more slowly than expected, and its risk adjustment was accrued on September Wakely data. In July Molina cut Marketplace by $1.50/share to a -$0.75 FY loss and said it took a 'conservative pick' on risk adjustment while its view was 'evolving'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marketplace was the line behind the July 2026 -9.7% (a $1.50 cut that wiped out a $1.50 Medicare raise) and the 2025 resets (-16.8% in July 2025 and -17.5% in October 2025).
evidence.why_not_priced: It came out this morning, and ELV's stock fell on the quality of its beat, so no positive ACA read-through shows in MOH today (down intraday). If the market had priced a better Marketplace risk-adjustment true-up at Molina, MOH would have outperformed ELV today; it did not. This is a proxy: Molina said its retained ~280K members are adversely selected and higher-acuity than the market, which is why it is sized below the Medicaid read.
evidence.independence: Same Elevance call as the Medicaid finding, different line. Centene's Q2 10-Q booked a $481M benefit from the final 2025 risk-adjustment transfers (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001071739/000107173926000153/cnc-20260630.htm), but that is benefit year 2025 and already in Molina's Q2.

evidence.text: UnitedHealth's Q3 2026 (2026-10-13) showed a consolidated MCR of 88.4% vs 89.9% a year earlier and ~89.9% expected, with $610M of favorable prior-period reserve development, and it raised FY adjusted EPS to at least $20.50. Community & State Medicaid membership fell to 6.695M (-10% YoY, -85K in the quarter).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sector read-through. UNH rose ~4.5% on its print, and MOH is up 6.3% over the month against a flat provider group (Yahoo preview).
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: MOH has run +13.6% over 20 days, including a +3.8% day on 2026-10-12 attributed to managed-care sentiment (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Molina+Healthcare+Gains+as+Investors+Weigh+Sector+Tailwinds+and+Near-Term+Catalysts). What is left is the reserve-development signal that cost trend in 2026 dates of service is coming in benign, which would also show in Molina's prior-period development. Sized small because it is priced.
evidence.independence: Separate document from the Elevance findings. https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/expect-molina-healthcare-moh-q3-063750358.html confirms the UNH reaction and MOH's run.

A Q3 that lands 'on guide' at ~$0.70 would read as a small miss on the headline. That is under 2% of shares and not crowded. 25-delta skew -4.86 vol points: calls are bid over puts ('upside paid'), and put/call OI is 0.54. ATM IV is 120.7% on the 23 Oct expiry, with an event-implied move of 8.3%. Tape: -13.2% over 20 days, -1.9% over 5, -45% from the 52-week high (a June peak), realised vol 50%. The drawdown runs alongside an AI and optical sector rotation (SOX -4.3% on 14 Oct after the Broadcom and Intel CEOs' AI-funding warnings; COHR, LITE and AAOI down 5-9% on 14-15 Oct).

evidence.text: Ericsson's Q3 (15 Oct, after Nokia last spoke on 23 Jul) printed net sales of SEK 59.5bn against an LSEG consensus of SEK 55.4bn (+7%), with organic growth of +7% and Networks sales +17% q-o-q on India and Japan. That is a direct read-through to Nokia Mobile Infrastructure (Q3 consensus ~EUR 2.8bn, +2% y-o-y; Inderes) and to the revenue line, where consensus sits only at the midpoint of Nokia's 3-7% q-o-q guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nokia's own prints (rebuilt, because the baseline's 8 'moves' are share-transfer 6-Ks, verified for 15 Oct and 8 Sep): Q2 on 23 Jul 2026 beat on comparable operating profit (EUR 434m) and fell about 5-7% on the soft Q3 guide (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/nokia-s-massive-ai-orders-overshadow-soft-guidance-bofa-sees-upside/cZZYLRvR7Uu). Q1 on 23 Apr missed revenue, raised the Network Infrastructure guide and rose about +6.5% (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/NOK/q1-2026/, approximate). This name trades on guidance and orders, not on reported-quarter revenue.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nokia's revenue consensus (EUR 5,054m on 15 Oct, 5,058m on 19 Oct) did not move after Ericsson's beat, and NOK fell in the week after Ericsson rose 9-12%. Had the read-through been priced, the consensus would sit in the upper half of the guide and NOK would have tracked ERIC. Jefferies framed Ericsson's strength as specific to Ericsson ('lack of AI exposure'), and part of Ericsson's Networks margin was retroactive IPR revenue, which limits the transfer to Nokia.
evidence.independence: Ericsson's own release (https://www.ericsson.com/en/press-releases/2026/10/ericsson-reports-third-quarter-results-2026) and RTTNews (https://www.rttnews.com/3699316/ericsson-q3-profit-drops-sales-rise-simplifies-operating-structure-stock-gains.aspx) confirm the numbers; that is the same event, not an independent pointer to Nokia. It is a peer proxy: Nokia has not confirmed anything since 23 Jul.

evidence.text: Ciena (3 Sep, after Nokia's Q2) reported backlog of $8.5bn (+$0.8bn q-o-q), expected above $10bn by fiscal year end, said one month into FQ4 it had booked nearly as much as in all of FQ3, and guided FY27 revenue +30% or more. Inderes adds that Ciena is raising prices 10-20%. Nokia's own FY26 Optical+IP guide of 18-20% (Network Infrastructure 12-14%) looks conservative against that, which raises the odds of a Network Infrastructure guide raise or strong AI and cloud order commentary.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Network Infrastructure guide raise at Q1 (23 Apr 2026) coincided with roughly +6.5% despite a revenue miss. At Q2 the guide was held (only technically raised) and the stock fell about 5-7%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Inderes's 19 Oct preview still carries Network Infrastructure at about +14% and Optical+IP at 19%, inside the existing guide, and FY consensus EBIT of EUR 2.40bn sits only slightly above the midpoint. Had a raise been expected, consensus would sit at or above the top of the range. The optical complex sold off 5-9% on 14-15 Oct on AI-funding fears, so the market is discounting optical demand rather than extrapolating Ciena.
evidence.independence: Inderes preview (https://www.inderes.dk/analyst-comments/nokia-q326-preview-blikket-rettet-mod-ai-ordrer-og-vaekstforventninger-for-de-kommende-ar) notes that Nokia's optical and IP targets look cautious against peers and cites Ciena's price increases. Also https://app.sentisense.ai/stories/ciena-posts-record-q3-revenue-on-ai-demand-as-stock-fluctuates-09032026 (Ciena fell 10% on an in-line guide, a reminder that the sector sells in-line numbers).

evidence.text: Component and memory cost inflation is a margin risk to the outlook. Ericsson's Q3 release (15 Oct) says 'component costs are a headwind to gross margin next year'. TrendForce puts CPU, DRAM and SSD at 68% of a benchmark notebook BOM in Q3 2026, against 45% in Q1 2025. Nokia already guided Mobile Infrastructure gross margin down to 44-46% in Q3 from 49% in Q2. If Nokia echoes Ericsson on 2027, or softens its 'meaningful' Q4 step-up (FY consensus needs about EUR 1.2bn in Q4), the outlook line takes it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 (23 Jul 2026): a held FY guide plus a soft Q3 guide took the stock down about 5-7% despite a profit beat. Q4 2025 (Jan 2026): a cautious 2026 guide made the stock slip (https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/nokia-oyj-HEL:NOKIA/news/nokia-slips-as-cautious-2026-guidance-disappoints-019e6a08-038d-7e20-9861-50fa3e020c0a/).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Ericsson said it publicly and still rose 9%, and Inderes lists component availability and price increases as a watch item. What is not priced is a quantified Nokia number. FY consensus sits slightly above the guide midpoint, so a margin caveat on Q4 or 2027 lands against a bar that assumes the hockey stick.
evidence.independence: TrendForce memory BOM data (https://www.implicator.ai/trendforce-memory-costs-laptop-prices/) is an industry proxy. The Inderes preview also cites Ciena's price increases and supply only balancing by 2028. Nokia itself flags component costs only as a generic risk factor (Q2 release).

evidence.text: The comparable operating profit bar sits above the company's own guide. Nokia guided Q3 comparable operating profit 'roughly flat' on Q2's EUR 434m (software revenue timing), while consensus is EUR 453m (Infront, 21 analysts) and EUR 462m (FactSet), so a print at guide (Inderes: 435) is a 4-6% miss against consensus even with revenue in line.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's profit beat (EUR 434m) did not protect the stock (down about 5-7% on guidance). Q1's in-line profit with a guide raise rose. Profit lines in the reported quarter have been secondary to the guide and orders.
evidence.why_not_priced: Wire consensus sits above the guide, so the sell-side bar has not adopted the company's 'flat' signal. If it had, consensus would read about EUR 435m as Inderes does. The two consensus sources disagree by EUR 9m, and Nokia beat its own conservative Q2 framing, so this is sized small.
evidence.independence: Inderes preview (Infront consensus 453 vs Inderes 435; https://www.inderes.dk/analyst-comments/nokia-q326-preview-blikket-rettet-mod-ai-ordrer-og-vaekstforventninger-for-de-kommende-ar). It shares the Inderes document with the orders finding below but rests on a different number.

evidence.text: AI and cloud order intake is likely to fall q-o-q from Q2's EUR 2.8bn: Nokia itself warned the Q2 level should not be expected every quarter, and half converts within 12 months. Into a tape where the AI-funding fears of 14 Oct (SOX -4.3% that day, about -12% on the week; optical names down 5-9% on 14-15 Oct) have made AI orders the headline line, a sequential decline reads badly even if it was guided.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: record AI and cloud orders (EUR 2.8bn, sales +105% y-o-y) did not stop a 5-7% fall on the soft guide and a broad tech sell-off. Q1 2026: AI and cloud sales +49% plus a raised Network Infrastructure guide rose about +6.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The company warning is public, so a modest decline is partly expected. The macro framing is new since mid-October and is a proxy (company-to-hyperscaler transmission unconfirmed). Ciena's comment that one month of FQ4 bookings nearly matched all of FQ3 argues the other way, which is why the band is wide. If fully priced, the skew would not have calls bid.
evidence.independence: AI-funding sell-off: https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/semiconductor-stocks-ai-funding-squeeze-1825976 and https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/15/optical-stocks-extend-slide-as-money-rotates-into-defensives-applied-optoelectronics-falls-6-coherent-drops-7-lumentum-slips-5/ (proxies). The order warning shares the Inderes document with the EBIT-bar finding.

evidence.independence: Baseline skew -4.86 and put/call OI 0.54 (sealed baseline).

evidence.text: Positioning into the print is long-leaning after a news-less rally while the option market still pays for downside. The stock rose from a 52-week low of about $155.3 (2026-10-07) to $173.49, +9.7% in 5 sessions. The +7.4% day on 10-15 came on volume about 45% below average and was attributed only to a Zacks expected-beat note. Skew is +3.08 (downside paid) and the put/call OI ratio is 5.88. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: the last 7 prints were -6.55, -2.37, -14.48, +0.91, +3.00, -6.66 and +1.01. The two 2026 beats (Q1, Q2) were sold, and the in-line or confirm-guide quarters of 2025 moved about +1 to +3.
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-up itself prices an expected beat that the consensus EPS ($3.37, -0.6% y/y) does not carry, so the stock now needs more than an in-line print. If the market had priced the risk of 'in-line, guide reconfirmed', the 5-day run-up would not sit at +9.7% on thin volume with no company news.
evidence.independence: The baseline skew (+3.08) and P/C OI 5.88 come from a separate source (Yahoo option chain, in the sealed baseline). evidence.text: Pentair, the largest pool-equipment supplier to POOL, cut channel inventory with 'major channel partners' by about $170m in Q2 (Pool segment sales -42%), guided Q3 Pool sales down 23-25%, and expects channel inventory to normalise by the end of Q3. BNP's analyst tied this to POOL, Pentair's largest customer. This implies POOL bought far less equipment in Q3, which can weigh on purchase-volume vendor incentives and gross margin. POOL's CFO said on 2026-07-23 that nothing Pentair reported changed the guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin has been the line: Q2 2026's 30bp margin decline plus a lower GAAP guide went -6.55%, and Q4 2025's miss went -14.48%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EBIT of $172m equals the guide's mechanics, with gross margin at -30bp. If the market priced a destock-driven hit to vendor incentives or absorption, Q3 EPS consensus would sit below the guide-implied run-rate and not on it. Pentair's Q3 numbers (due 2026-10-27) are not yet out, so the size of the Q3 destock at POOL has not been confirmed.
evidence.independence: Pentair Q3 guide of Pool -23-25% (Pentair Q2 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000042/q22026pressrelease.htm). Barclays' Fluidra downgrade cites POOL's 'record-high inventory' and US destocking (https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/fluidra-sa-MCE:FDR/news/barclays-cuts-fluidra-to-quot-equal-weight-quot-on-us-destocking-concerns-019e6dd4-a4f0-7d70-852c-93fc9b27145d/). Counterweight: lower inventory also means stronger Q3 operating cash flow, and the CFO explicitly excluded any Pentair effect from the guide (https://www.webull.com/news/15277450926826496). This is a proxy: no POOL document quantifies it.

evidence.text: Summer 2026 (June-August) was the hottest on record for the contiguous US per NOAA: +0.4F over the prior record, a record August, record-warm summers in AZ, NM, UT and CO, and record August heat in southern Florida. Hot weather lifts chemical and maintenance volumes, POOL's largest category, in Q3. POOL's CFO called July 'pretty much on point', and Q2 sales in CA, TX and AZ were down mid-single digits.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on weather. The Q3 2025 print (sales +1%, EPS beat) went +0.91%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue growth of +1.5% is below the 2-3% H1 pace even before any weather effect, so a volume lift from record heat would show up as a revenue beat. The market has not credited it: the stock fell to a 52-week low on 10-07, a month after NOAA published.
evidence.independence: NWS Tampa summer summary (https://www.weather.gov/media/tbw/climate/summaries/Aug_Summer2026_final.pdf) shows Florida sites in the top-ten warmest. Counterweight: Leslie's reported comps -6.2% to 2026-07-04 with weather and traffic cited (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821806/000119312526346961/lesl-ex99_1.htm), and chemical price deflation continues (Q2 chemicals -2%). This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed.

evidence.text: Leslie's, the largest pool-supply retailer and competitor to POOL's independent-dealer customers, filed prearranged Chapter 11 on 2026-09-30, closing 76 of 900+ stores, after comps of -6.2% in the quarter to 2026-07-04. That is market share freed for POOL's dealer and retail customers, and it is the first call on which management can comment on it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: there is no prior competitor bankruptcy in the window.
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock fell to its low a week after the filing, so the market treated it as a demand signal rather than a share-gain one. Any positive read needs management to say so on the call. The benefit falls mostly in Q4 and 2027.
evidence.independence: Leslie's Q3 FY26 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821806/000119312526346961/lesl-ex99_1.htm), a different document from the same company. It cuts both ways: weak consumer pool demand (negative) and an ailing competitor (positive). Any POOL receivable exposure to Leslie's is unknown.

evidence.text: John Watwood, CEO since mid-2026, presents his second print and the last before his first full-year guide. The FY guide is $10.87-11.17 with consensus at about the midpoint.
