evidence.text: The 8-K filed 2026-07-22 (Items 1.01/1.02) amends the PowerCo program. The maximum aggregate PowerCo will pay is $75.4M 'inclusive of amounts paid to date' (it was up to $131M), cost-reimbursement SOW No.1 was terminated on 2026-07-16, and further payments depend on milestones (cell delivery and validation over the next two years). Q2 customer billings were $10.8M, of which $10.4M was PowerCo collaboration cash. Billings were roughly $41M from 2025 through H1 2026, so the remaining program headroom is about $34M or less over two years, about $4M a quarter. evidence.text: The guide arithmetic leaves a low bar: first-half comps were about -0.6% (Q1 +0.5% on $3.59B, Q2 -1.5% on $4.54B), so the FY comp guide of -1% to flat implies a second half of about -1.4% to +0.6%, and the CFO's base case was 'modest sequential improvement' from Q2's -1.5%; the -1.1% Q3 consensus and the $1.93 FY EPS consensus both sit at the bottom of what the company guided to, against the toughest compare of the year (Q3 2025 comp +3.9%, July the hardest month).

evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the consensus already sits at the low end, which is the market's way of discounting the guide. evidence.text: Q3 deliveries were 486,532, 5.3% above Tesla's own IR-compiled consensus of 461,974 (24 analysts) and above the Bloomberg 466k and Visible Alpha 469k figures. Production was 464,391, so roughly 22k units came out of inventory. That points to revenue at or slightly above the ~$27.8B bar, and to working capital helping FCF against a Hudson-cited consensus of about -$1.1B.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose +4.65% on the 10-02 delivery release (baseline). At the Q2 print on 2026-07-22, revenue beat ($28.24B against ~$25.7B) with deliveries 18% over consensus, but adjusted EPS missed ($0.33 against $0.51-0.55) and the stock fell -14.52% (baseline). A revenue beat has not paid on its own here.
evidence.why_not_priced: The delivery count is fully priced (the stock rose 4.65% that day). What may not be is the revenue translation: the revenue consensus of $27.6-28.0B sits BELOW Q2's $28.24B, even though Q3 delivered more cars and slightly more storage. If the market had marked revenue up, the Visible Alpha and Zacks revenue numbers would sit above Q2, not below it.
evidence.independence: Company release with production and deliveries (https://www.financialcontent.com/article/bizwire-2026-10-2-tesla-third-quarter-2026-production-deliveries-and-deployments). Teslanorth gives the same consensus (https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/02/tesla-q3-2026-deliveries/). These describe the same document, not independent evidence.

evidence.text: Energy storage deployments were 13.7 GWh, 13.8% below the 15.9 GWh consensus and only +1.5% QoQ against 13.5 GWh. That points to energy revenue below models. Partly offsetting, Q2 energy gross margin of 20.4% carried a ~$240M one-time vendor-cell warranty charge plus the loss of a >$200M Q1 tariff benefit, so energy margin should rebound in Q3 without that charge; the 17.7% consensus GM likely already assumes this.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history on storage alone. The energy margin swing from 39.5% to 20.4% was part of the Q2 miss that fell -14.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The deployment miss has been public since 10-02 and is largely priced. The margin direction is the open question: if the market expected a margin miss in energy, the GM consensus would not sit 90bp above Q2.
evidence.independence: Q2 energy warranty and tariff detail is from the Q2 call coverage (https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/XBUL:TL0/transcripts/8973402, 2026-07-22). The miss and the deployment number share the delivery release with finding 1.

evidence.text: The WSJ reported on 2026-10-15 that Mike Snyder, VP of energy and charging and head of the Megapack business since Oct 2024, has stepped down, with AJ Booth succeeding him; Tesla has not commented. That leaves a leadership gap in the segment that is supposed to carry margin, in a quarter when deployments missed by 14%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance in the baseline. The stock fell -1.29% on 10-15, the day the report circulated, with the Roadster event that evening.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is in the wire but has not been addressed by the company. The call is where it either gets explained away or gets attached to a weaker energy outlook. If the market were pricing it, energy-margin expectations would have been cut since 10-15; no evidence of that was found.
evidence.independence: Stocktwits relays the WSJ report (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/Markets/Equity/tesla-energy-chief-mike-snyder-reportedly-exits-as-elon-musk-pushes-ai-and-robotics-pivot/cZxhOgzRBrZ). It is the same underlying report.

evidence.text: Regulatory credit revenue fell to $146M in Q2 2026 from $439M in Q2 2025 (-67%) and from ~$380M in Q1. The 10-Q adds new language: 'recent governmental and regulatory actions have restricted certain regulatory credit programs', and only $220M of credit RPO is due over the next 12 months. Credits are therefore stuck near $50-150M a quarter, at near-100% margin, against $400M+ a year ago.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The credit collapse was part of the Q2 margin miss (-14.5%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Q2 already reset the level. The residual is a y/y profit headwind of ~$300M that keeps the y/y EPS comparison ugly and a sub-1% credit contribution to margin. If any part of the bar still assumed a credit rebound, the consensus GM would sit above 17.7%.
evidence.independence: Electrek ties the drop to CAFE penalties being zeroed out by statute (https://electrek.co/?p=476867).

evidence.text: China: CPCA September domestic retail was 64,837, down ~9% y/y and the fourth straight monthly decline; YTD domestic is down ~12% while exports doubled. Tesla is running October discounts of CNY 5,000 on Model 3 and CNY 7,000 on selected Model Y. That is a Q4 price-and-margin headwind the call has to address.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean line history. JPMorgan cited US and China weakness when cutting its Q3 delivery forecast in September.
evidence.why_not_priced: Small discounts in one region get little attention next to a global delivery beat. If it were priced, the Q4 GM estimates would have been trimmed after the 10-02 beat; instead, consensus EPS fell for Q3 only. Sized net of Europe, which is growing (finding 6).
evidence.independence: Drive Tesla Canada carries the same CPCA data (https://driveteslacanada.ca/?p=125285), so it is the same data set.

evidence.text: Forward demand outside China looks strong. EU+EFTA+UK registrations Jan-Aug were 191,787, +43.3% y/y (ACEA); September registrations rose 62% in France and 38% in Sweden. Autoevolution reports Tesla has largely run down its inventory, with delivery estimates for most models and markets now beyond January 2027. Tesla raised US Model Y upper-trim prices in May, and the Cybertruck Standard sold out for 2026. Pricing power should support the Q4 commentary.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. Q2's stronger volume did not stop a -14.5% reaction on margins.
evidence.why_not_priced: Wait times past January 2027 mean supply-constrained demand. That is a margin and Q4 delivery statement, not just a Q3 one. The previews focus on margin compression and capex; if backlog were priced, Q4 delivery and margin estimates would have risen after 10-02.
evidence.independence: European registration data from Finviz (https://finviz.com/news/397487/tesla-registrations-rise-across-several-european-markets-in-september) is a different source from the autoevolution backlog claim. evidence.text: Tesla held 11,509 BTC, with digital assets at $674M on 2026-06-30 (10-Q). Bitcoin rose ~43% in Q3 2026 (from ~$58.5k to ~$84k), so the fair-value gain is roughly $290M pre-tax, about $0.06-0.08 a share. Few EPS models include it. It is unclear whether Tesla's 2026 non-GAAP includes it: in 2026 the 'restructuring and other' line stayed at $0 despite a $334M H1 BTC loss.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3 2025 an $80M BTC gain went largely unremarked in the reaction (+2.28% at that print).
evidence.why_not_priced: A mark-to-market gain is rarely in consensus. If it were modelled, the adjusted EPS consensus would have risen as bitcoin rallied through Q3; instead it fell 3c in 30 days. It has no path to guidance, so it is sized as a fraction of the same dollars as operating profit.

first_hunter_context.bar: Company guide Q3 2026 net sales $1.10-1.14B, non-GAAP EPS $1.21-1.27 (8-K 2026-08-06, https://investors.ttm.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-336163/d132953dex991.htm); consensus about $1.13B revenue (Benzinga) and EPS $1.22 (Benzinga) / $1.25 (Yahoo, 4 analysts, range 1.24-1.26), so two sources roughly agree inside the guide. The implied Q4 bar is the hard one: FY2026 'approximately $4.4B' less Q1 $846M, Q2 $1,004M and Q3 midpoint $1,120M leaves about $1.43B organic for Q4 (+28% q/q), which the Q4 guide must meet; the Q4 guide will also be the first to include Epiq (closed 2026-09-30) and possibly STG/ILFA, so its comparison to consensus is not clean.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 4,128,561 shares, 3.97% of float, 2.13 days to cover, record date 2026-09-30, up 20% from 3.44M on 2026-09-15 (MarketBeat/FINRA, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/TTMI/short-interest/, fetched 2026-10-21). Not crowded. Skew_25d +8.28 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 1.03, event-implied move 9.19%, ATM IV 87.8%. Tape: -19.85% over 20 days, -54.5% from the 52-week high, closed $93.88 on 2026-10-16 after a sector AI-hardware selloff, spot $100.85 at seal. CEO bought 10,000 shares in the open market on 2026-08-25 at $111.77.

evidence.text: TTM beat its own revenue guide by a wide margin last quarter: Q2 2026 net sales $1,004M against a $930-970M guide (+5.7% vs the $950M midpoint) and $962M consensus, with non-GAAP EPS $0.99 vs $0.82-0.88 guided; on the Q2 call management said M+N (asymmetric AI PCB) full production had started with yields 'better than expected', about $600M of M+N in H2 split one-third Q3 / two-thirds Q4, and margin improvement in Q3 and Q4. A repeat beat of similar size puts Q3 revenue near $1.16B against the $1.13B consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (bmo 2026-08-06): a 5.7% revenue beat plus a FY raise to $4.4B bought +3.89%. The +15.07% (2026-04-29) and +16.63% (2025-04-30) moves came with strong guides; three of the seven prints in the baseline (2026-02-04 -3.78, 2025-10-29 -2.44, 2025-07-30 -3.04) were sold, so a beat on the reported quarter alone has not reliably paid.
evidence.why_not_priced: The consensus sits inside the guide ($1.13B / $1.22-1.25) rather than at the level of the Q2 beat pattern; if the street had carried a repeat 5% beat, consensus would sit above the top of the guide ($1.14B) and the stock would not be 54% off its high with downside skew bid.
evidence.independence: The company's own Q2 release (https://investors.ttm.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-336163/d132953dex991.htm), the same quarter's document set, so this is one source family; peer read in the separate Amphenol/Gold Circuit finding.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-12, inside the quarter's reporting gap, TTM announced $400M of incremental 'Rapid-Ramp' brownfield capacity for N+M asymmetric AI interconnect at four China plants and Penang, on top of the $1.2B 2025-2029 plan, with the CEO stating 'the rapid growth in demand requires us to make rapid capacity increases' and citing ongoing discussions with hyperscaler, data-center and networking customers. That is company-level evidence that demand runs above the capacity behind the $4.4B FY outlook, which supports a Q4 guide at or above the implied ~$1.43B and the 2027 framework.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raises drove this name's two largest up moves (+15.07% 2026-04-29, +16.63% 2025-04-30); the Q2 FY raise from 'at least $4B' to $4.4B bought +3.89%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock fell from about $126 on 2026-10-01 to $93.88 on 2026-10-16 after the announcement, in a sector AI-hardware selloff, so the market read the capex as cash out rather than as a demand signal; if the demand were priced, the stock would not be at -20% over 20 days with puts bid into the print. The release gave no numbers and deferred detail to the Q3 call, so the call is where the demand gets quantified.
evidence.independence: Q2 call (separate document) said M+N yields beat plan and backlog was $901M 90-day, +81% y/y, book-to-bill 1.49: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001116942/000119312526337923/d142017dex992.htm

evidence.text: On the Q2 call management reaffirmed 15-20% organic growth for 2027 and 2028 and said a longer-term plan would follow 'next quarter', i.e. on or around this Q3 call; a first multi-year target set (plus first commentary on Epiq/STG/ILFA/Ophir integration) is new information on the line this stock trades on, with the sign unknown and the size large.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior long-term-target event in the baseline; guide-driven prints moved 15-17% when strong.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street cannot model a target that has not been given; the 87.8% ATM IV and 9.2% event move are consistent with the market expecting a large move but the skew does not tell which way; a reaffirmed 15-20% organic plus acquisitions would put 2027 revenue well above what a $100 stock at roughly 20x the 'approach $5.00' FY26 EPS discounts.
evidence.independence: Same call transcript as finding 1 (shared document); no separate source confirms the timing of the plan.

evidence.text: The Q4 guide will be the first to consolidate Epiq Solutions ($1.1B cash, 17.4x synergy-adjusted 2027 EBITDA, closed 2026-09-30, funded by $300M TLA + $800M TLB + $500M 6.75% notes due 2034) and possibly STG/ILFA, with net leverage stepping from 0.9x to about 2.3x at close and Ophir Optics ($650M on the revolver, announced 2026-10-19, closing Q2 2027) on top; the company itself says Epiq is moderately dilutive to non-GAAP EPS in 2027. Roughly $1.6B of new debt at ~6.5-7% is about $25M a quarter of interest, so a headline Q4 EPS guide can land below an organic street number even if the business is on plan.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Epiq announcement (2026-08-17/18): the stock fell, with auto-alerts citing -5.7% pre-market and -10.8% in the session; no prior print has carried an acquisition-diluted guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock has already de-rated hard on the M&A and leverage (54% off the high). What is not priced is the mechanics of the first consolidated guide: consensus for Q4 on aggregators (Q3 EPS $1.22-1.25) was formed on an organic basis, and a revenue guide jumping on acquisitions while EPS guidance absorbs interest can read as a miss on the wire. Financing answer [sizing note removed]: the money buys defense/RF businesses at a high multiple, not the AI ramp, so this is a negative on the guide line, sized small because the de-rating already reflects it.
evidence.independence: Epiq deal terms and leverage path in the 2026-08-17 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1116942/000119312526353148/d375900dex991.htm); notes terms in the 2026-09-24 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1116942/000119312526401013/d186334d8k.htm); Ophir funding on the revolver (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/ttm-technologies-to-acquire-ophir-optics-for-650-million-93CH-4957311).

evidence.text: CEO Edwin Roks bought 10,000 shares in the open market on 2026-08-25 at a weighted $111.77 (about $1.1M), bringing his direct holding to 64,814 shares; it was the only open-market purchase found in the 2026 Form 4 record, after insider sales under 10b5-1 plans near $210 in June.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: none in the baseline
evidence.why_not_priced: Public for two months and the stock has fallen about 10% since, so it is mostly a statement about management confidence rather than unpriced information; a small weight only.
evidence.independence: none

evidence.text: Kingboard raised FR-4 laminate and prepreg prices repeatedly through Q3 (+15% on 2026-06-16, +15% on 2026-07-06, +10-20% on 2026-08-28, another +15% on 2026-10-13, citing fiberglass cloth and copper foil), and TTM itself flagged tight lower-end laminate supply on the Q2 call; that is input-cost pressure on the non-AI half of the mix (automotive 8%, parts of MI&I) for Q3 gross margin and the Q4 guide.
evidence.source_date: 2026-08 (URL path) with the timeline updated to 2026-10-13
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin has been rising (non-GAAP 21.9% in Q2, +100bp y/y); no print in the baseline turned on margin compression.
evidence.why_not_priced: A secondary-source industry proxy; TTM's high-end AI materials are said on the call to remain available, and the company guided margin up, so this is a small offset rather than a call. Net of the rest: the 40-49% data-center mix and 32-37% A&D are on different materials and pricing.
evidence.independence: TTM's own Q2 call comment on tight lower-end laminate (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001116942/000119312526337923/d142017dex992.htm); proxy, not confirmed in TTM's numbers.

evidence.text: Counterparties that spoke after TTM's Q2 report point to intact AI board demand: Amphenol guided another mid-teens sequential increase in IT datacom for Q3 (2026-07-29) and Gold Circuit Electronics, an AI-server PCB peer, posted a record NT$10.0B July revenue (+77% y/y) and said Q3 would rise sequentially on delayed shipments and new Taiwan/Thailand capacity.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Data Center & Networking grew 91% y/y in Q2 and was 40% of sales, guided to 49% of Q3; the stock bought the Q2 print +3.89%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Peer demand is public and the sector sold off anyway in mid-October on AI-financing worries; this is a proxy that says the demand side of the guide is not the risk, sized small.
evidence.independence: Gold Circuit July 2026 revenue (https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/6418300); proxy, not TTM's number.

evidence.text: The 20-day drawdown (-19.85%, to $93.88 on 2026-10-16) coincided with a sector-wide retreat in AI optics and hardware names (Coherent -7% on 2026-10-15 and -5.7% on 2026-10-16, Lumentum, AAOI) attributed to CoreWeave financing worries and hot inflation data, not to a TTM-specific operating event; short interest rose 20% into 2026-09-30 but stays at 4% of float.
evidence.source_date: 2026-10-16 (Friday after the 2026-10-15 selloff; date per article text, not URL)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 printed +3.89% after a July drawdown of about -38%; a de-rated stock bought a clean beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Positioning itself is priced by definition; the point is that the de-rating is sector and M&A, so a clean operating print has room, while the skew still says the option market expects downside. Small.
evidence.independence: Earlier July drawdown also attributed to valuation/profit-taking rather than a company event (https://www.itiger.com/news/1106986794).

evidence.text: Ophir Optics ($650M, ~10.3x FY2027 EBITDA, revolver-funded) closes in Q2 2027 pending Israeli/Romanian approvals; its accretion and leverage effect land after the window.

first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 revenue ~$5.91B / adj EPS ~$2.40-2.42 (iTiger 2026-10-15 https://www.itiger.com/news/1199935814 ; Hudson Labs 2026-10-05 https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/texas-instruments-q3-2026-earnings-preview-txn-results ; Earnings Whispers consensus $2.40, whisper $2.46, rev $5.93B https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/TXN), which equals the company guide midpoint ($5.65-6.15B, EPS $2.23-2.57). Q4 2026 bar: Benzinga snippet $5.68B / $2.26 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TXN/earnings-forecasts, undated, snippet_only) and FY2026 revenue consensus $21.91B / EPS $8.49 on stockanalysis.com (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/txn/forecast/), which less Q1 $4.8B + Q2 $5.463B + Q3 $5.91B implies Q4 ~$5.74B. The two Q4 sources roughly agree (-3% to -4% q/q). The buy-side Q4 bar is unsourced and probably higher.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 20.44m shares, 2.25% of float, 3.2 days to cover, up 3.5% from the prior settlement, record date 2026-09-30, published 2026-10-09 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/TXN/short-interest/). Not a crowded short. 25d skew is +9.67 vol points (downside paid) and front-expiry put/call OI is 0.47 (call-heavy OI). The event-implied move is 6.78%. Run-up is +2.6% over 5 days and +5.65% over 20 days. Spot is 13.3% below the 52-week high (~$334, set around June-July) and roughly back at the level after the July print ($277 open / $294 prior close on 2026-07-23).

evidence.text: Independent Taiwan analog series kept rising after TXN last spoke on 22 July. Silergy (6415, a China-centric power-analog peer) reported September revenue of NT$2.511bn, +3.9% m/m and +50.7% y/y, on 8 Oct. Its Q3 total is NT$7.27bn (YTD Sep 18.141bn less H1 10.869bn) against a H1 quarterly average of ~NT$5.43bn. That is consistent with TXN printing in the upper half of its $5.65-6.15B guide rather than at the $5.91B consensus midpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $5.46B vs $5.24-5.25B consensus (~+4%) with an above-seasonal guide, and the stock fell -3.1% close to close (baseline; https://www.tradingpedia.com/2026/07/23/texas-instruments-stock-drops-despite-upbeat-forecast/). Q1 2026 beat-and-raise: +19.4%. The reported-quarter beat alone has not been paid reliably.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus still sits exactly on the guide midpoint ($5.91B), so the street has not marked Q3 to the upper half. A Taiwanese monthly filing in Chinese is not in the US preview copy. The whisper ($2.46 vs $2.40) shows the buy-side expects some beat, and a beat inside the guided range is what the company told the market to expect, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Separate source: WT Microelectronics (distributor) reportedly posted a record September at about NT$215.9bn, +9% m/m (snippet_only, LinkedIn repost: https://tr.linkedin.com/in/cem-urgup-8557a724). WPG August revenue was +80.5% y/y (https://www.wpgholdings.com/news/detail/en/revenue/26042). These are proxies, not TXN numbers. TXN's China exposure is 22% of revenue by HQ (10-Q).

evidence.text: The published Q4 2026 bar (~$5.68-5.74B, about -3% q/q from a $5.91B Q3) looks stale against peers that guided after TXN last spoke. ADI (19 Aug) printed $4.02B against a $3.9B guide and guided Aug-Oct to $4.2-4.4B vs $4.08B consensus, with its CFO saying demand 'continued to strengthen ... throughout the third quarter'. Microchip (6 Aug) guided the Sep quarter +8% q/q with book-to-bill 'well above 1'. TXN itself said price increases execute in Q3 and continue into Q4. A Q4 guide midpoint near flat (~$5.9-6.0B) would beat the published bar by 3-5%. TXN's own Q4 habit is -5% to -7% (e.g. Q4 2025 guide midpoint $4.40B vs Q3 2025 $4.74B), so the published bar already assumes above-seasonal.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide surprises dominate this name. Apr 2026, strong Q2 guide: +19.4%. Jan 2026: +9.9%. Jul 2026, Q3 guide above the $5.61B consensus: -3.1% (profit-taking after a ~70% YTD run). Oct 2025, weak Q4 guide: -5.6%. Jul 2025: -13.3%.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market had priced a flat-to-up Q4, the published Q4 consensus would sit near $5.9-6.0B rather than $5.68-5.74B, and the stock would not still be at its post-July level ($288 vs a $277 open on 23 Jul) while peers re-rated on raises. The skew (+9.7 downside) says the options market leans to a disappointing guide or a 'peak cycle' read, so the sign is against the skew. The reason the market may be wrong: the counterparties' own guides (ADI +7%, MCHP +8%) plus a pricing tailwind landing in Q4 are company-level numbers, not inference. The buy-side bar is unsourced and likely above the published one, so the size stays well below the implied move.
evidence.independence: Microchip guide: https://quartr.com/events/microchip-technology-inc-mchp-q1-2027_3etrCKBt (2026-08-06). NXP Q3 guide raised to ~$3.75B midpoint, but the stock fell 5.5% (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nxp-semiconductors-nasdaqnxpi-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-07-28/). TXN pricing commentary: Hudson Labs preview (2026-10-05). Q4 bar: Benzinga snippet and the stockanalysis FY figure. Different documents, one thesis.

evidence.text: Price increases are hitting the P&L for the first time this cycle: TXN said pricing was flat in H1 and increases execute customer by customer in Q3 into Q4 and 2027, mainly in Analog (82% of Q2 revenue at $4.365B). With fabs under-loaded (inventory 196 days, 'loadings adjusted further in Q3'), gross margin is set for upside against the 61.8% Q3 consensus (Q2 printed ~61.4%).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 gross margin rose ~300-340bp q/q and EPS beat by ~11%, yet the stock fell -3.1%. Margin beats have not been paid on their own.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: consensus GM already assumes +40bp q/q and the EPS whisper sits $0.06 above consensus. What is not visible is the size of the price uplift, which TXN has not quantified. Sized small and mostly inside the guided EPS range.
evidence.independence: ADI raised prices again from 13 Sep 2026 (TrendForce, https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/08/13/news-adi-reportedly-set-to-raise-prices-again-on-september-with-military-chips-facing-up-to-30-hike/), which shows industry-wide pricing power. Q2 GM is from TXN's 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000152/txn-20260630.htm).

evidence.text: Reaction function and positioning: TXN and its closest peer both sold beat-and-raise prints this cycle (TXN -3.1% on 22 Jul, NXP -5.5% on 28 Jul). TXN has gone sideways since July despite peer raises. The option market pays +9.67 vol points for 25d puts over calls, and short interest rose 3.5% to 2.25% of float (3.2 days) into the print. A good print with a merely in-line or seasonal Q4 guide is likely sold again.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Of the last 7 prints, 3 rose. Both 2025 Q3 (-5.6%) and 2026 Q2 (-3.1%) fell despite fundamentally fine quarters.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the priced side, filed as the counterweight. The skew is the market's own statement, and the risk is that the bull findings above are what the buy-side already holds (whisper above consensus, 8 of 9 directional analyst calls bullish per iTiger). It is not a crowded short (2.25%), so there is no squeeze mechanism to shrink it further.
evidence.independence: Short interest: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/TXN/short-interest/ (2026-09-30 record). NXP reaction: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nxp-semiconductors-nasdaqnxpi-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-07-28/. Skew is from the sealed baseline.

evidence.text: On 17 Sep 2026 TXN pre-announced a 7% dividend increase ($1.42 to $1.52 quarterly), larger than last year's ~4% step ($1.36 to $1.42). It is subject to the board's October meeting and framed as returning all FCF over time, a signal of management's FCF confidence with capex tracking the low end of $2-3B.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction attributable to the dividend line. FCF-per-share commentary was part of the Apr 2026 +19.4% print.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since it was public on 17 Sep. The formal declaration at the October board meeting likely comes with the release and confirms it. Filed small because a larger raise than last year is a management tell on Q4 cash.
evidence.independence: Capex tracking the low end and FCF/share above the $8 target: Hudson Labs preview (2026-10-05). Shares the FCF thesis with nothing else in this file.

evidence.text: Personal electronics is constrained by memory. TXN guided only modest Q3 sequential growth in that segment because of memory shortages, and NXP said mobile would decline y/y in Q3 on component constraints. This caps one end market (roughly a mid-teens share of revenue) into Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history. Net of the rest of the company, industrial (+30% y/y), data center (2x y/y) and auto (mid-teens) dominate the mix, so this segment drag is small.
evidence.why_not_priced: Company-disclosed, so mostly priced. Filed because a Q4 guide comment extending the memory constraint would trim the above-seasonal case.
evidence.independence: NXP Q3 commentary on mobile constraints: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nxp-semiconductors-nasdaqnxpi-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-07-28/

evidence.text: This is the first earnings call with Julie Knecht as CFO (effective 1 Aug 2026, succeeding the retiring Rafael Lizardi), and therefore her first Q4 guide. A first-time CFO guide carries some risk of a conservative midpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history for this CFO. The 8-K of 2026-06-02 (item 5.02) documents the transition.
evidence.why_not_priced: The transition is public. The guide-conservatism effect is an inference with no TXN-specific evidence, so it is filed small.
evidence.independence: EDGAR 8-K item 5.02 dated 2026-06-02 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000097476&type=8-K). Same fact, no independent pointer to the direction.

evidence.text: China MOFCOM anti-dumping probe into US analog interface and gate-driver ICs (TXN named). It opened 2025-09-13, was normally due by 2026-09-13 and is extendable by six months to ~2027-03-13. No preliminary or final determination was found in search. China was 22% of TXN Q2 revenue by HQ.
